body.statement: Suppose \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q=(1-\alpha)/2\). Uniformly on \(\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\) has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\eta\). For deterministic \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), there is a Rademacher immediate-outcome plus finite hidden-sign delay family in the same experiment for which \((\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau)/s_{T,0}\Rightarrow N(-u,1)\) and \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to u>0\); for every fixed \(c'>0\), the limiting coverage of \([\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\) equals \(\Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1\). Hence \(c_\eta(u)\) is attained for symmetric intervals at the phase boundary.
body.justification: The result converts the phase boundary into an attained local experiment rather than a conservative bias comparison.
body.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár supply the generic bounded-bias Gaussian calibration, while delayed-bandit work does not derive or attain its bias ratio in the adaptive observed experiment.
body.consumer: This gives trial statisticians the correct critical value when the endpoint-tail and exploration exponents meet at the nonzero-shift boundary.
